summary: Page 4 (Vol. 34, No. 29) of the National Negro Weekly runs James Weldon Johnson's 'Views and Reviews' column plus a right-rail gossip/news-clippings column that includes a one-paragraph item crediting the Red Bank Echo (a New Jersey Black newspaper) for a story about a Baltimore man who had a five-inch horn removed from his forehead, a case the item jokingly calls more distinctive than encephalitis lethargica. Surrounding items in that same clippings column cite the Detroit Leader, the Christian Recorder, the Galveston City Times, and other Black papers reprinting notable items; the main page also covers Norfolk Virginian-Pilot editorializing on Southern peonage/lynching investigations, a K.K.K.-focused Searchlight rebuttal, the New York State Guard armory fight, the 'Jim' hero/bank-robbery story, and the Coleman murder-case appeal in the Bronx.
